findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch name as an argument, not shell source
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `main; command`, `exec` runs the appended command with the process's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation passed the value as one Git argument without shell interpretation.

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as a single argv element instead of shell source
findings.body:
`exec` interprets the branch through a shell, so valid Git ref characters can introduce additional process transitions. For example, `topic;touch${IFS}pwned` causes `git show topic` followed by `touch pwned`, rather than showing that branch. This permits arbitrary command execution and makes the returned child represent the shell lifecycle rather than the intended Git process.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid passing branch names through a shell
findings.body:
Any caller-controlled branch containing shell syntax, such as `main; rm -rf target` or `$(command)`, executes arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. The previous `execFile` call passed the branch directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch name as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, so a caller-controlled branch such as `HEAD; rm -rf /target` executes arbitrary commands with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile()` implementation treated the branch as a single Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
